question: What is the primary pump of the cardiovascular system?
explanation: The heart functions as a muscular double pump that drives blood continuously through the vascular network. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: How does the cardiovascular system assist in body temperature regulation?

options.A: By adjusting blood flow to the skin
options.B: By producing sweat directly from the atria
options.C: By shivering the major coronary arteries
options.D: By releasing bile to cool core organs

explanation: Vasodilation and vasoconstriction near the body surface help dissipate or conserve heat. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which layer of the heart wall is primarily responsible for contraction?
explanation: The myocardium is the thick muscular middle layer that generates the force needed to pump blood. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the clinical significance of the endocardium being a smooth endothelial lining?

options.A: It anchors the fibrous skeleton to the bony thorax
options.B: It prevents abnormal blood clotting inside the heart chambers
options.C: It allows the heart to absorb oxygen directly from chamber blood
options.D: It secretes hormones to regulate systemic blood pressure

explanation: A smooth internal lining minimizes turbulence and keeps platelets from adhering and forming unwanted thrombi. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h2)

question: Through which valve does blood pass when leaving the right ventricle?
explanation: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary valve into the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h3)

question: A patient diagnosed with mitral valve stenosis will experience impaired blood flow directly into which chamber?
explanation: The mitral valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle, so narrowing restricts flow into the left ventricle. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h3)

question: Where do the coronary arteries originate?

options.C: The base of the ascending aorta

explanation: Coronary arteries branch off the ascending aorta right above the aortic valve to supply the heart muscle. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is an independent coronary circulation necessary for the heart?

options.A: The myocardial wall is too thick for chamber blood to nourish it by diffusion
options.B: Coronary vessels operate at a higher pressure than the systemic aorta
options.C: The endocardium blocks all nutrient transfer from the ventricles
options.D: Blood inside the heart chambers lacks oxygen entirely

explanation: Diffusion is only effective over very short distances, requiring dedicated blood vessels inside the heart muscle. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is known as the natural pacemaker of the heart?
explanation: The SA node initiates electrical impulses fastest, establishing the normal sinus rhythm of the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the functional importance of the delay at the atrioventricular node?

options.A: It protects the SA node from electrical burnout
options.B: It increases the blood pressure inside the coronary sinus
options.C: It prevents the ventricles from contracting at the same time
options.D: It allows the atria time to empty their blood fully into the ventricles

explanation: A slight pause ensures ventricular filling is maximized before the ventricles contract. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h5)

question: What mechanical event directly causes the first heart sound (lub)?

options.A: Opening of the aortic and pulmonary valves

explanation: The first heart sound marks the beginning of ventricular systole when AV valves snap shut. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT true regarding diastole in the cardiac cycle?

options.A: It represents the phase of active ventricular muscle contraction
options.B: It is the period when the heart chambers fill with blood
options.C: Coronary blood flow is optimal during this phase

explanation: Contraction is systole, whereas diastole is the relaxation and filling phase. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h6)

question: How is cardiac output calculated?

options.A: Heart rate multiplied by stroke volume
options.B: Heart rate divided by total peripheral resistance
options.C: Stroke volume divided by blood pressure

explanation: Cardiac output depends on how fast the heart beats and how much blood is pumped with each beat. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h7)

question: What term describes the resistance the ventricles must overcome to push blood into systemic arteries?
explanation: Afterload refers to the arterial pressure or impedance that ventricular muscles work against during ejection. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h7)

question: Which blood vessels are responsible for the direct exchange of nutrients and gases with body tissues?
explanation: Capillaries have extremely thin walls composed of a single endothelial layer that permits diffusion. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h8)

question: Why do veins require internal valves whereas most arteries do not?

options.A: Capillary beds require backflow protection before fluid enters the venous system
options.B: Veins carry oxygenated blood which flows more sluggishly than deoxygenated blood
options.C: Venous blood pressure is very low and must be kept moving toward the heart against gravity
options.D: Arteries need to stretch to withstand high pressure generated by ventricular systole

explanation: Low pressure in veins combined with gravity requires valves and muscle contractions to prevent backflow. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h8)
